analysis: The code snippet is a private static method that writes a line to an OutputStreamWriter. The only API call is writer.write(line). No pre-call checks or validations are performed; the method simply synchronizes on the writer object and then calls write. The synchronization does not prevent I/O exceptions. After the call, there is no catch block. The documentation for write declares only IOException. Therefore, the exception conditions are not avoided in any way.
remark: IOException can be triggered by the underlying output stream, e.g., if the stream is closed, the file system is full, or any other I/O error occurs. No checks are performed before the call to avoid these conditions.
